chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَكَى بَعْضُ الثِّقَاتِ بِنَيْسَابُورَ: أَنَّهُ خَرَجَ لِإِسْحَاقَ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ مِنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ تَوْقِيعٌ: …

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: One of the Thiqat in Naysabur relayed that: there came out a signed rescript from Abi Muhammad (peace be upon him) to Ishaq b. Ismail saying: …

chunks.arabic_text: وَيَا إِسْحَاقُ اقْرَأْ كِتَابَنَا عَلَى الْبِلَالِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ الثِّقَةُ الْمَأْمُونُ الْعَارِفُ بِمَا يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ، وَاقْرَأْهُ عَلَى الْمَحْمُودِيِّ عَافَاهُ اللَّهُ فَمَا أَشْهَدُ لَهُ بِطَاعَتِهِ …

translations.en: O Ishaq – read this letter of ours to al-Bilali – may Allah be well pleased with him – for he is the Thiqa and trusted one, the one who recognizes what is incumbent on him, and read it too to al-Mahmudi – may Allah give him health – our praise of him is because of his obedience …

en.summary: This rescript from Imam Abi Muhammad (peace be upon him) to Ishaq ibn Ismail underscores the Shia emphasis on *tawqi'* (imperial rescripts) as a primary source of authority during the Minor and Major Ghaibah. It specifically validates the trustworthiness (*thiqa*) and religious knowledge (*arif*) of al-Bilali, while praising the obedience of al-Mahmudi, illustrating the hierarchical transmission of religious directives through trusted intermediaries.
en.seo_question: What qualities did the Imam attribute to al-Bilali and al-Mahmudi in this rescript?
